messages:
Sam (Hiring): Maya accepted! Shes in London and needs H-1B consular stamping. Wants to start remote ASAP. Can we onboard her as a US employee while she stamps?
Elena (People Ops): Short: not straightforward. We don't have a UK entity for US hires. Options: 1) Delay US employment until she re-enters on H-1B. 2) Use EOR in UK for interim employment. 3) Contractor (higher risk). Need payroll + legal input.
Maya (Candidate): Id like to start earlier to join sprint. EOR sounds fine if benefits/compensation roughly the same. Contractor ok but worried about taxes.
Priya (Immigration Counsel): Immigration note: H-1B approval doesn't equal ability to work in the US until consular admission. Working for Redwood while physically in UK is allowed, but if you bill Redwood as an independent contractor or direct employee on UK payroll without proper arrangements, there are tax/residency implications. Also avoid any actions that could be construed as unauthorized US employment once H-1B goes into effect. Recommend EOR or delayed US onboarding.
Noah (Payroll): Practical: We cannot put someone on US payroll while they are physically working in UK without local entity. If we EOR, payroll partner will withhold UK taxes and handle local compliance. If we delay, we can onboard them in US payroll after entry; retro pay possible but need bank + tax docs quickly. EOR turnaround ~3 business days after signed forms.
Zoe (Global Mobility): I can get EOR quote and confirm which benefits (limited) we can mirror. EOR quotes typically include employer taxes and fees (~12-18%). We'll also map pension auto-enrolment requirements in the UK.
Elena (People Ops): If EOR: we'll open a limited benefits packet (wellness, equity deferral guidance), but core US benefits like 401(k) won't apply until US payroll. If contractor: no benefits, must sign contractor T&Cs and pass IC screening.
Priya (Immigration Counsel): Also add a short advisory for Maya re: H-1B timing and stamping timeline so she understands when status is active. Can draft and post here.
Maya (Candidate): Please send EOR cost ASAP. If numbers look close I'll go EOR. Prefer not to be contractor.
Sam (Hiring): Priority is retention and ramp. EOR preferred if cost reasonable.
Noah (Payroll): Action items: Maya to pick EOR vs wait by EOD tomorrow. Maya to provide UK ID and preferred bank info if EOR. Well need signed EOR docs.
Zoe (Global Mobility): I'll post EOR pricing + expected start date impact by EOD.
hr-bot: Tagging candidate-file: "h1b-eor-decision" and setting follow-up: 48 hours.
Elena (People Ops): Also note: benefits enrollment date will depend on when Maya is on Redwood payroll (not EOR). If EOR chosen, we'll create a plan to transition benefits when she moves to US payroll after stamping.
Priya (Immigration Counsel): Draft advisory: "Working remotely from the UK before H-1B entry is permissible, but the H-1B is effective only after consular admission. Using EOR prevents local tax exposure to Redwood; contracting can create tax/residency and unauthorized employment risk. We recommend EOR or deferred start." Will post final doc.
Maya (Candidate): Thanks everyone. I'll decide and respond by tomorrow morning.
Sam (Hiring): Thanks team. Let's keep candidate engaged with access to docs/repos regardless of status.
